clue.text: Soldier favoured fortification

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a favoured one is a pet, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A soldier is given the best defensive position on the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the top of a rampart, part of a defensive structure.

clue.text: Saint alert to change in image, benevolent but intrusive

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the next word

parts.note: pic is a short word for a picture or image

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters to be altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A watchful saint is depicted as kindly but meddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternalistic describes acting like a father toward people, protecting them while limiting their freedom of choice.

clue.text: Fence poorly, overcome by resistance

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overcome by something means sitting beneath it, so that piece goes first

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
poorly means unwell, or ailing

explanation.surface: A fencer, out of form, is beaten by the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like the sport; it is the barrier. Poorly is British for ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a barrier of upright bars, a kind of fence around a park or along a balcony.

clue.text: Shrub planted in location one approved initially

indicators.note: in sets the first piece inside the next word

parts.note: a point is a location
to plant is to set in the ground
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter only

explanation.surface: A bush is put into the spot that someone first gave the nod to.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with red leaf-like bracts, popular as a Christmas pot plant.

clue.text: Act so unnaturally in opera

indicators.note: unnaturally means not in the normal way, so the letters fall out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer is told to perform stiltedly in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' reads as a section of the opera, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's 1900 opera about a singer, her painter lover and the villainous police chief Scarpia.

clue.text: Yankee after discharge receiving new antagonism

indicators.note: after places the first letters following the ones named next, so they come at the end
receiving means taking something inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to discharge is to emit
N is the standard abbreviation for new
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American soldier, after being discharged, is met with fresh hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: N sits inside EMIT, giving ENMIT, and the Yankee's Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is the state of being hostile or opposed to someone, which is what antagonism names.

clue.text: Depression during bad year without question

indicators.note: during means within the span of something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bad means evil
a dent is a small depression in a surface
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Low mood through a terrible year is beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low spirits, but it is a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidently means plainly or obviously, as clear as can be, so beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Squalid plan

definitions.meaning: first ...: poor and shabby, as in ... streets

explanation.definitionFit: Mean describes shabby, run-down surroundings, and to mean to do something is to intend it.

clue.text: Symbolic drink label, collector's first

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
EMI is a famous record label

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: first letter only

explanation.surface: A collector prizes the meaningful label on a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'label' looks like a sticker on the drink, but it is a record company.
explanation.definitionFit: Totemic means serving as an emblem, like a totem that stands for a clan, so it is representative.

clue.text: Film that's funny has apt slips in it

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or out of order, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedy is praised for having its pratfalls in just the right places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film that's funny' reads as one phrase meaning a comedy, but only 'Film' defines; 'funny' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Is Spinal Tap is a 1984 mockumentary movie by Rob Reiner about a hapless rock band.

clue.text: All income, finally put on record with force, below average figure

indicators.note: in a down clue, below places everything else beneath the piece that follows

parts.note: par is the average or normal level
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter only
a log is a written record
to ram is to force

explanation.surface: Every penny earned is written down, and the result is a below-average sum.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on record' sets the first letters above LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A parallelogram is a four-sided geometric shape with two pairs of parallel sides, a plane figure.

clue.text: Control said to be restored

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
said means stated

explanation.surface: Someone's words about authority are reported to have been brought back into force.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reinstated is to be put back into a former position or condition, the same as being restored.

clue.text: Part of problem irritating ruler

indicators.note: part of tells the solver that only a portion of the following run of letters is wanted

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A monarch is bothered by a nagging difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, the title of the ruler in several Gulf states.

clue.text: Refresh ratio given wrongly

indicators.note: something given wrongly is set out in error, so the letters come out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a mixture ratio to be corrected after a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' looks like part of the indicator, but its letters are needed for the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to give fresh energy and life, the same as making someone feel refreshed.

clue.text: Progress in skill with jargon

indicators.note: in places the first word's letters inside the letters of the next one

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
to go is to make progress

explanation.surface: Getting better at a craft comes with learning its specialist vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the private slang of a particular group, close in meaning to jargon as specialist language.

clue.text: Bad action in laboratory brought about, relating to plant study

indicators.note: brought about is a turning round, as a ship comes about, so the word runs the other way
in places the rebuilt letters inside the other word

parts.note: lab is the usual short form of laboratory

indicators.note: bad suggests the word is spoilt and must be rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mishap in a lab has consequences for some research into plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical is the adjective for botany, the scientific study of plants, so it relates to plant science.

clue.text: English fan transformed into animal in celebratory event

indicators.note: into sends the reworked letters inside the next word

parts.note: a beast is an animal

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: E for English plus the word as written

explanation.surface: An English supporter turns wild at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is British slang for a jolly party or a celebration with plenty of food, originally a works dinner.

clue.text: Unreal yarn I concocted, taking wise men in

indicators.note: taking means admitting something inside, so the mixed letters hold another piece
concocted means made up or cooked up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity story

explanation.surface: A storyteller admits making up a tale that features the wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in the mind, so it is not real at all.

clue.text: Mad liar struggling to become officer

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crazy fibber is working hard to gain a commission.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the most senior naval commander, a flag officer in charge of a fleet.

clue.text: Foolish sign painter leaving odd bits out

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered positions keeps only the second, fourth and later even ones

parts.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A silly signwriter skips some of the letters on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes something senseless or silly, lacking any intelligence, which is what foolish means.

clue.text: Leave teacher to support a veto

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporter holds up from below, so that piece comes last

parts.note: taken as written
a veto is a ban
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A lecturer backs a proposal to block something.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or go away from someone or something for good, which is to leave it.

clue.text: Boring master

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to bring under control, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'master' reads as a noun after an adjective, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tame party is dull, and to tame a wild animal or a fear is to get the upper hand over it.

clue.text: Lover in trouble after a heartless lie

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is cut out of the word
after puts the first piece behind the ones named later in the clue

parts.note: taken as written
a lie is a fiction
ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A romantic partner is in difficulties after being caught out in a fib.
explanation.walkthrough: FICTION has seven letters, so its heart is the single middle T.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen devotee or enthusiast, a lover of some pastime such as opera or bullfighting.

clue.text: County in short leading second game

parts.note: Ches is the standard abbreviation for Cheshire, an English county
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A shire briefly heads the table in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game of strategy played with kings, queens and pawns on sixty-four squares.

clue.text: Member of family joined by good number

parts.note: a son is one member of a family
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A relative joins in with a fine performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks numerical, but it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a musical piece in a show or set, so any song performed can be called one.

clue.text: Terribly poor, in hole? Help, with hesitation, aggressive investor

indicators.note: with adds the remaining pieces on after the first
in sets the reworked letters inside the next word

parts.note: a crater is a hole in the ground

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
to help is to aid
er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A broke investor in a hole cries for help, hesitating as they go on the attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporate raider buys up stakes in companies to force a takeover, a famously hostile kind of financier.

clue.text: Departure following match

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 10f
a match is a light for a fire

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after a sports fixture has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game, but it is the thing you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight means running away or fleeing, so it is a sudden departure, as in taking flight.

clue.text: Bone from bird among quantity

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sum is an amount or quantity
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bone is picked out of a heap of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest joining the ribs.
